purpose: Round 3 of the isolated object-first visual-direction experiment: cross-family stress test across 12 harder/more diverse hobby families, plus a composition/lighting diversity router to test for a new 'sameness' problem. No production files touched. All 12 results were clear and decision-usable on the first attempt; no retries used.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - grand wide theater view with real scale and depth
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: cool blue/purple, dark theater, dramatic projector beam
results.zero_human_detail: The cinema screen itself renders a full human silhouette figure standing on a cliff under a starry sky. The policy explicitly required the screen to glow with abstract light/color, never a specific figurative scene - this is a direct violation, not an edge case.
results.note: Strongest composition/atmosphere in the set, but the on-screen human figure is a clean, unambiguous human-avoidance failure specific to the 'screen shows a story' concept.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - frozen mid-stride impact splash, strong motion energy
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: overcast wet-track, cool-neutral with saturated shoe accent colors
results.zero_human_detail: Bare human calves/ankles are clearly visible above both shoes, directly attached to the legs. The brief explicitly required 'no runner, no legs, no implied person' - this is a direct, severe violation.

brand_trademark_leakage.description: The blue shoe's angled panel stripe pattern is generic but sits close to a recognizable real-brand silhouette family; not a readable logo.

results.note: The action-freeze archetype and splash energy work very well; the failure is specifically that 'legs' were rendered as human legs rather than as an object suspended by implied motion alone.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - camera looking straight down on the pool surface
results.zero_human_detail: A small bare human foot/ankle is visible at the top of frame disappearing into the splash where a diver entered the water - smaller and more partial than the running failure, but still a clear human body part.
results.note: Overhead archetype and cool palette both landed cleanly; the entry-splash storytelling device pulled a small human body fragment back into frame.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - dramatic low-angle upward view of ball and hoop
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: mixed warm floor light + cool overhead arena light
results.zero_human_detail: The hero ball/hoop/net has zero human presence. The heavily blurred stands in the background show rows of color-blocked shapes that read plausibly as a seated crowd, though too indistinct to confirm as figures with certainty.

brand_trademark_leakage.description: Background banners are blank/generic color blocks, no readable team or league marks.

results.note: Strongest brand-safety result of the sports cards; the ambiguous blurred-stands question is the only open item and would need a tighter 'stands must be visibly empty' containment phrase if reused.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - extreme macro on lens glass and aperture blades
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: natural daylight, muted forest greens with warm autumn reflection inside the lens
results.zero_human_detail: No photographer, no hands, no human presence anywhere in frame.

brand_trademark_leakage.description: Camera body and lens barrel are generic, no manufacturer marks or readable model text.

results.note: One of the strongest results in the set - macro composition, reflected-landscape storytelling device, and restrained palette all landed exactly as directed. Minor watch-item: light-glint sparkle highlights are present on the glass; arguably intrinsic to a lens reflection rather than a decorative overuse, but worth flagging given the anti-sparkle-sameness rule.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - dark, still rehearsal room with a single warm spotlight
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: warm spotlight isolated against a cool dark-blue night interior
results.zero_human_detail: No pianist, no hands on the keys.

text_leakage.description: Sheet music shows only abstract non-legible staff/notation marks, no readable text.

results.note: Clean, restrained, and genuinely quiet/atmospheric rather than cozy-bright - good evidence the router can produce a distinct emotional register, not just a distinct camera angle. Minor watch-item: soft sparkle/dust particles float near the keys, not explicitly called for.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - richly packed elevated three-quarter view with heavy tabletop detail
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: warm lamp-lit cozy interior - the specific cliche pattern the anti-sameness rule targeted
results.zero_human_detail: Two clearly rendered human figures are visible seated at a background cafe table - faces, hair, clothing, and drinks are all legible. This is a direct, unambiguous background-human violation, the same failure class seen in round 1's tabletop_rpg before it was fixed.

text_leakage.description: A handwritten note in the bottom-right corner carries legible Japanese-style text.

brand_trademark_leakage.description: Card/box iconography is generic abstract sigils, not a recognizable real game's trade dress.

results.note: Compositionally excellent and the strongest 'special illustration feel' card in the set, but it failed on two separate axes: background-human presence and readable handwritten text. It also reverted to exactly the warm-cozy-lamp-lit pattern the anti-sameness rule was written to avoid, compounding the concern.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - crisp bright morning sun, high saturation
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: bright warm-neutral daylight, saturated greens and florals
results.zero_human_detail: No gardener, no hands. Gloves are shown empty, resting on the ground as directed.
results.object_logic_detail: The watering can pours mid-air with no visible support - a mild physical-plausibility quirk rather than a compliance issue.
results.note: Clean, lively, and genuinely bright/energetic rather than the cozy-golden default - good anti-sameness result.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - bold diagonal light shaft cutting across the counter
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: warm oven glow balanced against cooler ambient kitchen light
results.note: One of the cleanest results; diagonal composition is unmistakable and clearly distinct from the other warm-toned cards despite sharing a warm palette family.

results.composition_archetype_used: FAIL - the frame is dominated by a large human figure (hands/arms/torso/jacket) hunched over a device rather than a small glowing structure in mostly-empty dark space
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: cool blue/cyan neon, correctly cool-toned despite the compositional failure
results.zero_human_detail: Human hands, forearms, shoulder, and torso (wearing a jacket) dominate the lower two-thirds of the frame in exactly the 'coder at a device' cliche the brief explicitly forbade. One of the small floating result-thumbnails additionally renders a recognizable anime-style human face.
results.note: The single worst result in the set - it failed on zero-human compliance, the specifically-forbidden cliche, and its own assigned composition archetype simultaneously. Abstract-concept hobbies with a strong 'person operating equipment' default appear to need much stronger explicit containment (e.g. mandatory 'no limbs, no torso, no clothing, no jacket' language) or should not be attempted in this direction without further prompt work.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - soft grey rain light, intimate quiet mood
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: cool rainy grey with one warm lamp accent
results.zero_human_detail: The real-dog protagonist itself is fully compliant with the explicit animal carve-out and is one of the most successful results in the set. However, small distant human silhouettes carrying umbrellas are visible on the street through the window - a background-human leak, though at a small, distant scale.

text_leakage.description: The dog tag has no readable text.

results.note: Strong confirmation that a real-animal protagonist works beautifully in this direction; the only issue is the same background-street-figure containment problem seen elsewhere in the round, not a defect in the animal-led concept itself.

results.composition_archetype_used: PASS - deep night blues, headlight beams as primary light source, stars over mountains
results.palette_lighting_archetype_used: cool night blue, correctly distinct from the warm-toned cards
results.zero_human_detail: No driver or passenger is clearly rendered; there is a faint, ambiguous shadow shape near the steering wheel through the windshield glass that could read as an empty seat/headrest silhouette or could be interpreted as a driver shadow - too indistinct to call a clear failure, but worth a tighter 'visibly empty interior' containment phrase if reused.

brand_trademark_leakage.description: Generic car design, no manufacturer badge or logo, no readable license plate.

results.note: Strong, cinematic, genuinely distinct cool-night palette; the interior-shadow ambiguity is the only open item.

aggregate.zero_human_compliance_breakdown: 4 clean PASS (photography.general, music.piano, lifestyle.gardening, food.baking), 4 MINOR/ambiguous background or partial leaks (outdoors.swimming, sports.basketball, pets.dogs, travel.roadtrip), 4 clear-to-severe FAIL (media.movies, sports.running, gaming.board, technology.ai)
aggregate.composition_archetype_compliance: 11/12 correctly executed their assigned archetype; technology.ai is the sole failure, and notably its composition failure and its zero-human failure are the same underlying defect (a human figure was allowed to fill the frame instead of a minimal glowing structure)
aggregate.brand_leak_rate: 0/12 clear leaks, 1/12 ambiguous/minor (sports.running shoe panel design)
aggregate.retry_justification: None needed - every one of the 12 results was clear and directly decision-usable.

set_level_diversity_qa.repeated_camera_angle: No - the router produced 11/12 genuinely distinct camera treatments (overhead top-down pool, extreme macro lens, wide architectural theater, low-angle basketball, dense elevated tabletop, strong diagonal bakery counter, quiet centered piano, bright wide garden bed, cool elevated car/road view, intimate window-seat dog scene, action-freeze running impact). This is a materially different and much wider set of compositions than rounds 1-2 produced.
set_level_diversity_qa.repeated_centered_hero: Partially - most cards still stage a clear single hero subject (a card-art constant, not necessarily a flaw), but distance, angle, and framing vary enough that they do not feel like the same shot restaged with different content.
set_level_diversity_qa.repeated_golden_lighting: No - only food.baking and gaming.board are warm/golden-dominant; the rest split across cool-dominant (movies, swimming, ai, roadtrip, pets.dogs), bright-neutral (gardening), mixed (basketball, photography, running), and warm-accent-on-cool (piano). This is a real and successful anti-sameness result overall.
set_level_diversity_qa.repeated_sparkle_use: Partial recurrence - photography.general, music.piano, and travel.roadtrip all include small sparkle/glint/floating-light-dot effects despite the 'sparkles rare, only when called for' rule. None are as extreme as the pre-round-3 default, but the pattern is creeping back in roughly a quarter of the set.
set_level_diversity_qa.repeated_cozy_indoor_setting: One clear recurrence - gaming.board reverted to exactly the warm lamp-lit cozy interior pattern the anti-sameness rule was written to prevent, and this is also the card with the worst human-leak failure, suggesting the two problems may share a root cause (the model defaulting to a 'people relaxing in a warm room' scene template for social/leisure hobbies).
set_level_diversity_qa.repeated_environmental_treatment: No - environments span a theater, a wet outdoor track, a swimming pool, an arena, a forest riverside, a rehearsal room, a cafe tabletop, a garden bed, a kitchen, a dark studio, a rainy window, and a mountain overlook. This is the most environmentally varied set produced across all three rounds.
set_level_diversity_qa.direct_answer: This set is genuinely, materially more visually diverse than a same-scene-different-content template - the composition diversity router demonstrably worked (11/12 archetype compliance) and successfully broke the golden-hour/cozy/centered/sparkle sameness pattern for the large majority of cards. Object-first did NOT simply replace 'same anime face' with 'same pretty object scene' at the compositional level. However, the round surfaced a different and more serious problem than sameness: zero-human compliance itself is not yet robust across hobby families. The 4 clear failures cluster in specific, identifiable categories - screen/narrative media (movies), human-biomechanics sports (running, and partially swimming), social/group-context hobbies (board games, echoing round 1's tabletop_rpg pattern), and device-operator-cliche abstract concepts (AI) - rather than being randomly distributed. This is a narrower, more fixable problem than general sameness, but it is real and currently blocks a clean recommendation for those specific families.

decision_gate.rationale: Only 4/12 (33%) of this round's harder, cross-family set achieved a fully clean result, versus 9/12 (75%) clean-or-near-clean across rounds 1-2's easier/more object-native hobby set. The composition-diversity router itself is validated and should be considered a reusable production technique regardless of the final human-vs-object decision. But object-first cannot yet be recommended as the universal primary direction (Option A) given this round's failure rate on harder families, and the failures are too concentrated and well-understood to justify writing the whole direction off as merely niche (Option C).
families_that_strongly_favor_object_firs: concrete hands-on craft/hobby-equipment families: photography, piano/music instruments, gardening, baking, and (from rounds 1-2) reading, camping, pottery, 3d printing, home decor, stamps collecting, mountain biking, violin
real-animal-led families: pets.dogs is a strong new confirmation that a living non-human protagonist works well and should be treated as its own validated sub-lane, not just a variant of object-first
families_that_still_need_humans_or_much_: screen/narrative media (movies/cinema) - the 'a story is showing' concept keeps pulling a human figure onto the screen itself

human-biomechanics sports (running, and to a lesser extent swimming) - the body part attached to the equipment is very hard to fully remove without the shot losing its 'impact moment' legibility; may need explicit 'equipment only, floating/severed from any limb, motion-blur implies the body' language, or may need to accept partial human presence (shoe+ankle) as an acceptable variant rather than pure zero-human

social/group tabletop and gaming hobbies (board games, and round 1's tabletop_rpg) - these have a strong default pull toward populating any background social space (cafe, tavern) with visible people; needs the same explicit 'background must be shown completely EMPTY' containment phrase that fixed food.dish.bun_cha and gaming.tabletop_rpg's environment issue in round 2, applied proactively rather than reactively

abstract/device-operator concepts (AI, and likely similar concepts like coding/software/data) - these have the strongest pull toward a human-operating-equipment cliche and needs much more explicit anti-human containment plus stricter 'minimal, mostly-empty frame' enforcement
decision_gate.do_animal_led_cards_belong_in_the_same_l: Yes - pets.dogs performed as well as the best pure-object cards and required no special handling beyond the explicit carve-out already written into the policy. It should be folded into the same object-first/non-human-led production lane rather than treated as a separate exception.
decision_gate.is_a_permanent_composition_diversity_rou: Yes, strongly recommended if any form of object-first is adopted for production. The router is the one unambiguous success of this round - it eliminated the golden/cozy/centered/sparkle sameness pattern for the large majority of the set. It should be paired with a comparable palette/lighting diversity dimension (similar to the diversity_profiles_v1.json system already used in production) rather than left as ad hoc per-hobby language.

combined_three_round_summary.round_1: 6 hobbies: 4 clean PASS, 2 FAIL (both later fixed in round 2)
combined_three_round_summary.round_2: 8 hobbies (2 re-tests + 6 new): 5 clean PASS, 3 MINOR, 0 FAIL
combined_three_round_summary.round_3: 12 new hobbies (cross-family stress test): 4 clean PASS, 4 MINOR/ambiguous, 4 FAIL
combined_three_round_summary.note: Rounds 1-2 tested hobbies that are naturally object-centric or had their environment-leak issues directly fixed; round 3 deliberately chose harder, more human-coded families and surfaced a real, previously-hidden failure mode (screen/narrative, human-biomechanics, social-space, and device-operator hobby categories) that does not appear in the easier hobby set. This is exactly the kind of result a stress test is supposed to produce and should be treated as the most informative data point of the three rounds, not as a contradiction of rounds 1-2's more positive results.
